hook: A WSe2 photodiode on a lithium niobate chip receives 10 Gbit/s of visible-light data.
summary: The team built a lateral p-i-n photodiode from tungsten selenide coupled to a thin-film lithium niobate waveguide, using self-aligned doping and defect engineering for good contacts. It reached a 1.12 GHz bandwidth, about 492 mA/W responsivity, and 95.6% quantum efficiency at 638 nm. These are single-device results at one wavelength, so manufacturing yield is untested.
title: Thin-film lithium niobate waveguide-integrated p-i-n Tungsten selenide photodiodes with 10Gbit/s data reception
